name: Rhinoplasty simulation apps

card.summary: Morphing and 3D-imaging tools that preview how a nose might look after surgery; used by clinics and by prospective patients, with outcomes that are not guaranteed.
card.note: A simulated preview is an illustration, not a promise of surgical result.

quick.overview:
Rhinoplasty simulation software lets a person or a surgeon alter a photo or 3D scan of a nose to show a proposed change. Clinics use 3D cameras and planning software during consultations, and consumer apps offer similar photo morphing.

The topic appears in looksmaxxing discussion as a way to preview a result before surgery. This article is short because the available sources describe the clinical use only briefly.
quick.mechanism: Software maps the nose from standard photographs or 3D camera captures and lets the operator reshape contours digitally, so patient and surgeon can discuss the planned change.
quick.risks: The tools themselves are low-risk. The surgical result can differ from a simulation because healing, swelling and tissue behaviour vary between individuals; swelling after rhinoplasty can take a year or more to fully settle.

lead: Rhinoplasty simulation refers to software that predicts or illustrates how a nose might look after surgery. Surgical references describe 3D simulations and 3D cameras that capture and analyse the nose, allow modifications, and help surgeon and patient understand the anatomy and preview a potential result [1].

Standard clinical practice also includes photographs from several angles before and after surgery, which supply the images these tools work from [1]. Consumer apps that morph a photo exist alongside clinical systems, but the sources available for this article describe the clinical use only.
infobox: Illustrative preview of a proposed nose shape

paras: Rhinoplasty references describe software-based 3D simulation as a way to show existing deformities and plan the proposed approach, and 3D cameras as a way to inspect the nose and edit it virtually so both parties can discuss a likely outcome [1].
The same references note that healing differs between people and that swelling can take at least a year to fully diminish, which is relevant to how closely a preview resembles a final result [1].
